alignments.note: Substantival article with an adverbial modifier: it supplies the nominal expression and the relativizer, headed on the nominal word (rules 22, 32).
Adverbial predicate carries the supplied copula (rule 53).
Article governing an expressed head noun, realized by the supplied demonstrative determiner (rule 60).
The noun is rendered verbally; the supplied existential and the relativizer are its helpers (rules 7, 31), headed on the lexical verb (rule 17).
The English preposition realizes the dative case and rides with the pronoun (rule 21).
Second attributive article with no English realization (rule 23).

Distributive kata compressed to one English word: *dai-ly* spells the noun and realizes kata nowhere, so rule 45 rather than rule 35, headed on the governed word. Follows 2CO.7.10 `kata theon` -> *godly*, GAL.2.2 `kat' idian` -> *privately* and rule 45's own `kath' hena` -> *severally*. Reading the pair as aligned on the strength of *dai-* remains defensible.
The ASV supplies no determiner for the noun (rule 23).

The supplied case preposition rides with the quantifier, the article keeping a bare *the*: PHP.1.1 `pasin tois hagiois` -> *to all the saints* and REV.19.17 `pasi tois orneois` -> *to all the birds* are the identical configuration, and GAL.3.10 states the principle (the case preposition attaches to the leftmost English word of the phrase). Rule 21's shape has nothing standing between the preposition and the determiner.
